Lionel Messi Signs Off for Argentina With a Goal, Two Assists and a Lifetime of Memories

By  Sam Cohen
Published Oct 7, 2026, 7:26 AM GMT+1

Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents:
Try something different:

Lionel Messi was in tears before a ball had been kicked. By the end, he had given Argentina another goal and two more assists in his farewell appearance for his nation.

✕ Remove Ads

Argentina beat Benin 3-0 at the Monumental, with Messi playing all 94 minutes of his final game. Nicolás Otamendi and Nico Paz scored the other goals, both set up by their captain.

His children walked out beside him. A giant shirt formed part of the tribute. Benin’s players handed him a letter from their squad. Then came the anthem, and Messi struggled to hold back the tears.

A Goal and Two Assists Against Benin

The football stopped in the 10th minute. The crowd applauded its No.10, players shook his hand, and fireworks accompanied the tribute.

His first assist went to Otamendi, who was also making his final appearance for Argentina. After so many years together, the pair combined for the opening goal on the night they both said goodbye.

✕ Remove Ads

Messi then supplied Paz for Argentina’s second before scoring himself. All three goals came after the interval, following a first half in which Messi had four shots, two on target, and six touches in the opposition box.

There was no early substitution to arrange a separate ovation. He stayed on for the full 94 minutes, finishing with a direct contribution to every Argentina goal.

The Final Defeats and His 2016 Retirement

For years, his success at Barcelona was used against him. If he could do all of that for his club, why was it not happening for his country?

Argentina reached the 2014 World Cup final and lost to Germany. They lost the Copa América finals against Chile in 2015 and 2016. Before those came another final defeat, against Brazil in 2007.

✕ Remove Ads

Getting close was not enough to silence the criticism. Every defeat brought the questions back.

In 2016, Messi briefly walked away from international football, having lost three finals in three summers. His return meant trying again with a national team whose results were scrutinised alongside his achievements in Spain.

The comparison with Diego Maradona followed him throughout those years. Maradona had won the World Cup in 1986, and that became the achievement Messi was expected to match. League titles and Champions League success at Barcelona could not settle an argument centred on Argentina.

Messi was reaching finals, but the photographs at the end kept showing somebody else with the trophy. The 2014 tournament brought him a Golden Ball award as its best player, yet Argentina still left Brazil as runners-up. Individual recognition offered little relief when the team had come so close.

Copa America Success and the World Cup

✕ Remove Ads

The 2021 Copa America changed things.

Beating Brazil ended Argentina’s 28-year wait for a major senior men’s title. Messi finally had the international trophy that had been demanded of him for so long.

Under Lionel Scaloni, Argentina had become a team capable of helping their captain as much as he helped them. Messi remained their outstanding talent, but others could take responsibility when it mattered. That was crucial in Qatar.

Messi scored seven goals, supplied three assists and won the Golden Ball at the 2022 World Cup. Two of those goals came in the final against France.

The final finished 3-3, with Kylian Mbappé scoring a hat-trick for France. Argentina won the shootout 4-2, with Messi scoring his penalty. Argentina held their nerve. Messi finally had his World Cup.

Another Copa America followed in 2024. Messi had to come off in the final against Colombia and was left in tears on the bench, but Argentina still won the title. His teammates finished the job while their captain watched, unable to play any further part.

✕ Remove Ads

What World Football Will Remember

The Benin game marked his international farewell. His club career continues with Inter Miami, with his contract due to expire at the end of the 2028 MLS season.

At Barcelona, he scored 672 goals in 778 appearances and won 35 trophies. He left the club as its record scorer and appearance holder.

At club level, supporters became accustomed to seeing him collect the ball away from goal and carry an attack himself. Defenders had to decide whether to follow him into midfield or hold their position and let him turn. Getting close enough to challenge was only the start of the problem.

The goals were only part of the attraction. Messi could create the chance, play the final pass or finish the move himself. Sometimes he did most of that in the same attack.

✕ Remove Ads

For supporters growing up during his Barcelona career, watching Messi meant seeing a forward who was also responsible for much of the passing around him. He could drop towards midfield to receive, draw opponents out and then find the space they had left behind.

That is why the assists against Benin belonged so naturally alongside his goal. Across his career, deciding when to release the ball has been as important as knowing when to keep it. Argentina’s final evening with him included both sides of that game.

His rivalry with Cristiano Ronaldo also changed expectations. The numbers they produced season after season became the standard, even when almost nobody else could match them.

✕ Remove Ads

Against Benin, there was no trophy to lift. There was a crowd wanting to thank him, his children beside him, and one final match in the shirt.
